governance.note: Builds on the nyiso-33 ct-tempfloor keeper and adds a temperature-keyed downstate ST_GAS (gas-steam) local-reliability floor (--nyiso-st-reliability-floor, transmission.inject_nyiso_st_reliability_floor), the ST-fleet companion to the CT floor, plus two structural corrections it depends on and one benchmark-basis fix (Task A). MECHANISM: NYISO's downstate steam fleet (NYC zone J Ravenswood/Arthur Kill/Astoria; Long Island; Capital) runs a persistent in-city / cable-islanded reliability baseline an energy-only LP zeroes out (it imports cheaper CC instead), so the backcast under-runs ST_GAS. The floor is a persistent 24-hour baseline (base_24h) with an evening cooling hot-limb layered on over HB14-21 via maximum, applied PER UNIT, PRO-RATA (each in-pocket unit floored at frac x its OWN available capacity), keyed per zone to its load-center daily max temperature (Islip/Central Park/Albany, NOAA GHCN). TWO STRUCTURAL CORRECTIONS (both fix real methodology errors that were suppressing the costly in-city units, NOT residual tunes): (1) WHEN-AVAILABLE CF BASIS. frac is regressed on CF normalised by AVAILABLE capacity (nameplate net of the unit-outage derate), not by nameplate over all hours. The floor is applied as frac x pmax x availability, so the model already discounts outage downtime; regressing on the all-hours CF double-discounted it (the cool-day all-hours CF is itself deflated by the heavy NYC/LI steam downtime, then multiplying by availability again floored Astoria / Arthur Kill near zero). On the available basis these units run a steady ~0.3-0.4 baseline whenever committed (NYC temperature corr falls to ~0 — a flat in-city must-run), which frac x availability now reproduces (full baseline when available, zero on outage). (2) RAVENSWOOD OUTAGE ROUTING. Ravenswood (2500) is a mixed CC/ST facility classified ST_GAS in our bin, but CAMPD tags every unit CC_REGULAR, so its outage rows never reached the ST_GAS bin and it read near-fully-available (the floor then over-forced it to a baseload it never runs). data.outages._FLEET_GROUP_OVERRIDE routes plant 2500's outages to its ST_GAS bin so its model availability reflects the real downtime. CAPACITY-DERATE CHECK (this session, answering the derate question): the under-running in-city units are NOT ceiling-capped — they reach 0.66-0.92x nameplate in summer CAMPD with ample headroom; the under-run was a dispatch/availability/offer effect, addressed by the corrections above, not a derate to lift. GROUNDING: per-zone coefficients (transmission.NYISO_ST_FLOOR_COEFFS) regressed a priori from the measured per-zone CAMPD ST_GAS WHEN-AVAILABLE CF vs zone TMAX, pooled 2023-2025 (scripts/derive_nyiso_st_reliability_floor.py, archived data/raw/nyiso-weather/nyiso_zone_tmax_daily.csv): base_24h cool-day 24h available-CF p25, base_ev cool-day evening available-CF p25, cap evening available-CF p97 (clipped 0.95), slope evening hot-limb. Long Island base_24h 0.289 / base_ev 0.383 / slope 0.0406 / cap 0.891; NYC base_24h 0.391 / base_ev 0.432 / slope 0.0393 / cap 0.95; Capital hot-limb only. Flat/temperature-insensitive Upstate steam OMITTED. Set a priori before the solve; ST_GAS lands UNDER actual both scored years, NOT pinned (rules #11/#12). EFFECT — the HARD C1 fuel-mix now PASSES every gas class both scored years: ST_GAS 2023 -1.26(nyiso-32)/-0.24, 2024 -3.77(nyiso-33) -> -1.03 TWh (PASS); CC_REGULAR / CT_PEAKER PASS; dispatch_corr PASS (gas r=0.91/0.84/0.80); C5a CO2 in band all years. Plant distribution improved (Arthur Kill near-exact, Astoria / EF Barrett recovered, Ravenswood no longer over-forced); a zone-uniform floor cannot match every in-pocket unit's heterogeneous when-available CF exactly, so per-plant residuals offset within the C1 band (Ravenswood / Astoria slightly under, Northport / Port Jefferson slightly over). BENCHMARK-BASIS FIX (Task A, reporting only): NYISO solar actuals route to EIA-923 (actuals_source ISO-aware) — EIA-930 NYIS grid solar is a structural 0, so the dashboard now scores the model's ~2 TWh of dispatched utility-scale grid solar against the EIA-923 utility-scale total (2.05/2.90 TWh), not a spurious zero. The C3a/C3b/C3c price tradeoff is documented in the exceptions and kept per rule #1: the steam floor is a min-gen (must-run) representation that recovers the local-reliability ENERGY but adds inframarginal supply, depressing/flattening the marginal LMP rather than letting the units set a scarcity price.

_st_floor_status: The downstate ST_GAS under-run — the largest C1 (HARD) miss on every prior NYISO keeper — is CLOSED on the volume axis: ST_GAS 2023 -0.24 and 2024 -1.03 TWh both PASS, and every gas class is in C1 tolerance both scored years (fuelmix PASS). The remaining open items are all SOFT price criteria, the ledgered reserve-scarcity (ORDC) + min-gen-floor frontier: C3a mean LMP regresses (2023/24/25 -8.0/-19.4/-13.7%) and the C3b duration curve flattens (2024/2025 just out of band) because the must-run steam floor adds inframarginal supply and compresses the merit order rather than letting the units SET a scarcity price; the C3c >$300 tail is empty in the under-priced years (and slightly OVER in 2023, where the floor occasionally tightens supply). Closing the price side fully needs an ORDC / reserve-scarcity demand curve (units setting price in shortage) — the documented open frontier, confirmed non-closable with grounded inputs by nyiso-29/31, out of scope here. The price regression is the rule-#1 tradeoff for the HARD C1 volume gain and is kept, not chased (the floor lands ST_GAS UNDER actual, so it is not over-forced). 2025 per-class is preliminary-vintage (skipped). NET DETERMINATION: CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS — calibrated on the hard axes (per-class volume, system volume, dispatch correlation, CO2) with the price criteria as documented reserve-scarcity-frontier caveats.

exceptions.metric: C3a system load-weighted mean LMP vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. The per-unit min-gen ST_GAS floor recovers the local-reliability ENERGY (closing the HARD C1 miss) but adds inframarginal steam, depressing the marginal LMP rather than letting the units SET a scarcity price. The fuller fix is an ORDC / reserve-scarcity demand curve (the documented frontier, non-closable with grounded inputs per nyiso-29/31). Kept per rule #1; not chased (rule #12) — ST_GAS lands UNDER actual.

exceptions.metric: C3a system load-weighted mean LMP vs actual RT
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED (rule-#1 tradeoff; min-gen floor representation + reserve-scarcity frontier)
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. Largest depression because 2024 is the year the model most under-ran downstate steam, so the floor binds on the most idle in-city capacity. Same ledgered reserve-scarcity root cause (nyiso-29/31). Kept per rule #1; not chased — the base is the conservative cool-day available-CF p25 and ST_GAS still lands -1.03 TWh UNDER actual, so the price depression is the structural min-gen-floor consequence, not a too-high base.

exceptions.metric: C3c scarcity tail (>$300/MWh hour count) vs actual RT
exceptions.reason: SOFT criterion -> CAVEAT. The >$300 scarcity tail is the canonical reserve-scarcity (ORDC) frontier an energy-only LP cannot match without a reserve-scarcity demand curve. Here 2023 runs slightly OVER (the must-run steam occasionally tightens supply into a spike) rather than under; either direction is the same unmodelled scarcity-pricing mechanism (nyiso-29/31). Named, not chased (rule #12).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas family total vs EIA-930 grid (preliminary vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (preliminary EIA-923 / EIA-930 benchmark-basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2025 EIA-923 is the preliminary M-file (total under-reported); the C2 family gate falls back to the EIA-930 grid total, against which the model gas total sits ~-3.3% at its benchmark-basis floor. The ST_GAS floor is a within-gas reshuffle (steam up, CC down) and does not move the gas TOTAL. Not closable by an honest knob (rules #1/#11/#12).
